title: The Dreaming Bedrock Where Languages Merge

features.name: merged echo pool
features.desc-on-touch: you hear three voices at once, speaking words that don't belong to any one language; the stone hums beneath your feet

features.name: buried receiver
features.desc-on-touch: a rod transceiver half-sunk in terracotta soil, still breathing out broadcasts in languages that may be dreaming

features.name: linguistic fracture
features.desc-on-touch: words split at the edges; you see a letter transforming mid-stone, caught between two alphabets

features.name: dreaming figure
features.desc-on-touch: a stone form half-spoken, mouth open as if language is pouring out of it rather than in

features.name: merged archive stack
features.desc-on-touch: transliterated recordings layered in sandstone, each one shifting the meaning of the others, each one true

inscription: where words dream themselves into other words, and stone learns it was only ever listening

file.name: LinguisticLayers_TripleSpeech_Spliced.mp3
file.note: three field recordings at once: English, Yugambeh, and something that sounds like the archive speaking to itself

exits.label: back up through linguistic currents toward the original stone
deeper into redearth country where words become roots
